models.equation_text: EARN_{t+1} = γ_0 + γ_1 CFO_t + γ_2 NAC_t + γ_3 ABNAC_t + v_{t+1}

fixed_effects.details: The Table 2 joint system is estimated on firm-year observations; the paper does not report a fixed-effects dimension. The calendar years define the sample period, not a reported fixed effect.

standard_errors.details: Table 2 reports asymptotic standard errors for the unrestricted forecasting and valuation coefficient estimates. The source does not specify a robust or clustered correction.

evidence.quote: Asymptotic
Equation (2): EARN_t+1 = gamma_0 + gamma_1*CFO_t + gamma_2*NAC_t + gamma_3*ABNAC_t + v_t+1. The three RHS variables each have their own estimated slope, plus intercept gamma_0.

estimation_procedure.description: Equations (2) and (3) are jointly estimated as the Mishkin system by iterative generalized nonlinear least squares in two stages. The first stage leaves valuation coefficients γ*_q unrestricted from their forecasting counterparts γ_q. The second stage jointly re-estimates under rational-pricing equality constraints γ*_q = γ_q for individual components and reported combinations of components. The likelihood-ratio statistic compares constrained and unconstrained residual sums of squares, with degrees of freedom equal to the number of restrictions. Table 2 reports the unrestricted coefficient estimates and likelihood-ratio tests; the principal abnormal-accrual restriction is γ*_3 = γ_3. The fitted forecasting and valuation equations are separate records in the same estimation group.

evidence.quote: As in Mishkin (1983), I estimate equations (2) and (3) jointly using an iterative generalized nonlinear least squares estimation procedure, proceeding in two stages.
In the first stage, I jointly estimate equations (2) and (3) without imposing any constraints
I estimate equations (2) and (3) jointly in the second stage after imposing the rational pricing constraints
the sum of squared residuals from the constrained regressions in the second stage;
the sum of squared residuals from the unconstrained regressions in the first stage.

dependent_variable.name: SIZEAJR_{t+1}
dependent_variable.definition: Size-adjusted abnormal return for the 12-month period ending three months after the firm’s fiscal year-end: the firm’s annual buy-and-hold return minus the annual buy-and-hold return on its market-capitalization-based CRSP size decile. The size decile is assigned using market value of equity at the beginning of the calendar year when the return window begins. For a delisting during the year, liquidation proceeds are assumed reinvested in the market portfolio for the remainder of the year. Return variables are not deflated by assets.

evidence.quote: I use the 1995 CRSP monthly returns file to measure annual buy-and-hold returns (RETURNt) for the 12-month period ending three months after the firm’s fiscal year end.
If a stock is delisted during a particular year, I assume the liquidating proceeds are reinvested in the market portfolio for the remainder of the year.

I calculate size-adjusted abnormal returns (SIZEAJRt) as the difference between a firm’s annual buy-and-hold return and the annual buy-and-hold return for the same 12-month period on the market-capitalization-based portfolio decile (i.e., size decile) to which the firm belongs.

I use the CRSP size decile breakpoints to classify each firm into a size decile according to its market value of equity at the beginning of the calendar year in which the 12-month return period begins.
All variables except RETURNt and SIZEAJRt are deflated by beginning-of-year total assets (Compustat item #6).

statistics.units: Annual buy-and-hold return over the 12-month period ending three months after fiscal year-end; not deflated by assets. This is a raw return component of the prior-period size-adjusted return measure, not the retained t+1 outcome.

Equation (3): SIZEAJR_t+1 = alpha + beta*(EARN_t+1 - gamma_0 - gamma_star_1*CFO_t - gamma_star_2*NAC_t - gamma_star_3*ABNAC_t) + epsilon_t+1. The outer intercept is alpha; gamma_0 is the unstarred intercept inside the innovation. The coefficients gamma_star_1, gamma_star_2 and gamma_star_3 are estimated valuation parameters, not observed regressors. The equation is part of the same Nonlinear Generalized Least Squares system as Equation (2).

estimation_procedure.description: Equations (2) and (3) are jointly estimated as the Mishkin system by iterative generalized nonlinear least squares in two stages. The first stage leaves valuation coefficients γ*_q unrestricted from their forecasting counterparts γ_q. The second stage jointly re-estimates under rational-pricing equality constraints γ*_q = γ_q for individual components and reported combinations of components. The likelihood-ratio statistic compares constrained and unconstrained residual sums of squares, with degrees of freedom equal to the number of restrictions. Table 2 reports the unrestricted coefficient estimates and likelihood-ratio tests; the principal abnormal-accrual restriction is γ*_3 = γ_3. The fitted forecasting and valuation equations are separate records in the same estimation group.

evidence.quote: As in Mishkin (1983), I estimate equations (2) and (3) jointly using an iterative generalized nonlinear least squares estimation procedure, proceeding in two stages.

review_notes: Selected the Table 2 Mishkin system as the principal regression family. The source says the central question is whether the market prices Jones-model abnormal accruals consistently with their one-year-ahead earnings implications; the Mishkin system directly compares forecast and valuation coefficients. Retain the full earnings-component system (CFO, NAC, ABNAC) and its jointly estimated forecasting and valuation equations. The Table 3 hedge portfolio is corroborating portfolio evidence, not a regression family; alternative Jones measures and the refined-accrual/Table 4 analyses are sensitivity analyses.

The Jones-model construction is retained as a supporting fitted equation because its predicted values and residuals generate NAC and ABNAC in the Table 2 baseline system. Pre-1988 CFO is arithmetic construction, not another fitted model. Equation (2) estimated alone by OLS is discussed only for interpretation; that does not replace the joint generalized nonlinear least squares estimator used for Table 2.

Equation (1), equations (2) and (3), timing, scaling, and the equation (3) parameterized earnings innovation were checked against the supplied coordinator-verified mathematical transcriptions and rendered physical PDF pages 4, 5, and 7. No worker-generated mathematical transcription was used.

Unresolved for the supporting Jones equation: the paper does not identify the estimator used for its cross-sectional fits or report cell-specific N. Its predictor and residual definitions are reported and linked recursively to this fitted equation.
results_review_notes: Table 1 Panel A provides relevant descriptive statistics for retained earnings components and the prior-period form of the valuation outcome. Panel B contains contemporaneous correlations and is excluded as a correlation table.
The descriptive sample N is 56,692; the Table 2 system uses 51,579 observations after missing dependent-variable values are excluded.
Table 1 EARN_t and SIZEAJR_t are not exact summaries of EARN_{t+1} or SIZEAJR_{t+1}; timing differences are recorded without shifting means or sample sizes.
Table 2 Panel B shared rational-pricing diagnostics are represented as auxiliary rows on the existing valuation fit; the forecast and valuation coefficient fits remain the only result sets.
